literal_meaning: মাথায় সিঁদুর পরা (head on vermilion applied)
figurative_meaning_en: To remain a faithful wife until old age
example_sentences_in_bangla: তার মা সারা জীবন মাথায় সিঁদুর পরা ছিলেন, কখনো বিধবা হননি।
এই বাড়িতে সব নারীরা মাথায় সিঁদুর পরা অর্থাৎ স্বামীর প্রতি অনুরক্ত থাকেন।
example_sentences_in_english: Her mother wore sindur on her head throughout her life, never becoming a widow.
In this family, all women remain with sindur on their heads, symbolizing lifelong devotion to their husbands.
history: This idiom draws from the Hindu tradition where sindur (vermilion powder) is applied by married women in the parting of their hair as a symbol of marital status and devotion, originating from ancient Vedic rituals.
note: Primarily used in Hindu Bengali contexts to praise wifely virtue.
